V: Migraine with aura: Classic unilateral throbbing headache preceded by visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, family history
Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis: New severe headache, worse with Valsalva/leaning forward, risk factor of estrogen-containing OCP
Subarachnoid haemorrhage: Sudden severe headache with nausea/vomiting possible, though less likely without thunderclap description
I: Viral/aseptic meningitis: Headache, photophobia, nausea/vomiting without rash; could occur without high fever early
Acute bacterial meningitis: Similar rationale but fever/neck stiffness absent
N: Intracranial mass/brain tumour: Headache worse with position change, associated vomiting; patient anxiety due to friend’s history
Meningioma or low-grade glioma as tumour sub-types
D: Cervicogenic/tension headache: Worse with neck movement and work stress
Degenerative cervical spine disease causing referred headache
I2: Medication-overuse headache: Possible if frequent analgesic use after first episode
C: Congenital migraine diathesis (familial hemiplegic migraine variant)
A: Giant cell (temporal) arteritis: Unilateral headache but age <50 makes it unlikely
T: Occipital neuralgia secondary to repetitive strain
E: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension: Headache, visual symptoms, OCP use; often worse lying supine, typically in obese women
Hypothyroidism-related headache (family history, but patient denies thyroid disease)

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic constellation: unilateral throbbing pain, pre-monitory visual disturbances, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, similar prior episode, positive family history.
New severe headache, positional worsening, nausea/vomiting, and recent initiation of estrogen-containing OCP are textbook risk factors; presentation can mimic migraine.
Headache worse with movement and vomiting raise possibility, but lack of chronic progression or focal deficits makes it less probable.
Headache, photophobia, nausea/vomiting could fit, but absence of fever, neck stiffness, or systemic signs argues against.
OCP use and visual symptoms fit, yet typical demographic (obese female), positional pattern (worse lying flat), and papilloedema data are missing.
